From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 08:31:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in errors & throughput drop — triage notes

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Garbage collection/host OOMs ruled out on first pass.
- Error rate correlates with a percent increase in long-sequence requests for our largest retail model (seq length > 1,024 tokens) starting at 07:49 PDT.
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 72% to 21% across the serving pool — likely cache eviction due to a shifted prefix distribution.
- Autoscaler did not add nodes quickly enough due to insufficient autoscale headroom on the dedicated pool for this customer.

Immediate mitigations enacted (08:28–08:30):
- Applied an emergency routing rule to divert new AcroTech traffic to a warm spare pool in us-east-1 with a lighter sequence-length cap.
- Increased per-customer concurrency limit temporarily to allow additional throughput while we stabilize.

Working actions:
1) Roll back recent model rollout for AcroTech (candidate rollout from 02 Oct) — in progress.
2) Apply a longer TTL to the KV cache for this customer’s prefix sets.
3) Add cache-warming for top-traffic prefixes.

I’ll post logs and a short chronology in the shared doc. Marcus

[Inline: excerpt of metrics snapshot — errors by minute and KV hit-rate chart referenced in shared doc]

Summary (09:50 PDT):
- Issue: Rapid increase in long-sequence requests triggered cache churn and reduced throughput for your checkout endpoint starting 07:49 PDT. Error rate peaked at ~18% and median latency reached ~2s.
- What we did: Diverted traffic to a warm spare pool and temporarily raised concurrency limits (08:28–08:35). Rolled back the model rollout that coincided with the spike. K-V cache warming is in progress.
- Impact: Throughput is recovering; error rate down to ~3.5% and latency falling toward baseline. We will monitor the next 2 hours closely.
